claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires processing above 2300 °C to achieve densification.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens are susceptible to high-temperature oxidation.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens are susceptible to liquid plating-metal corrosion.
Equimolar Hf, Zr, Ta, Nb, and Ti on the metal sublattice can form a single-phase high-entropy diboride.
The resulting multicomponent diboride phase is compositionally disordered.
The proposed high-entropy diboride can be sintered at approximately 1700 °C.
Formation of the multicomponent diboride promotes enhanced densification at lower temperature.
High-entropy alloying produces grain-boundary characteristics that resist oxygen penetration.
High-entropy alloying produces grain-boundary characteristics that resist liquid-metal attack.
Lattice distortions and varied local bonding environments facilitate sintering at lower temperatures.
Compositional complexity leads to formation of a stable protective oxide scale during high-temperature exposure.
The high-entropy diboride has better oxidation resistance than ZrB2 and most of its other individual diboride components fabricated by the same procedure.
The high-entropy diboride maintains structural shape during oxidation exposure at 1500 °C.
At 1500 °C, the high-entropy diboride will have a notably lower oxidation rate than both high-temperature-processed ZrB2 and unalloyed ZrB2 processed near 1700 °C.
The high-entropy diboride will achieve density comparable to or greater than ZrB2 processed near 2300 °C.
The high-entropy diboride will achieve hardness comparable to or greater than ZrB2 processed near 2300 °C.
The high-entropy diboride will have greater liquid plating-metal corrosion resistance than both comparison ZrB2 groups.
The predicted improvements apply for sintering near 1700 °C and service temperatures up to 1500 °C.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome permits density and hardness to be comparable to the high-temperature ZrB2 control, whereas the falsification rule states that comparable mechanical integrity would falsify the hypothesis.
